before.title: Exact Helmholtz boundary representation with actual traces
before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded C-infinity domain of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let k>0 and x in Omega, and use the outgoing kernel $G_k$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]. A sufficient classical specialization is that u and f extend smoothly to an open neighbourhood of the closed domain and $(-\Delta-k^2)u=f$ there. More generally, retain the justified weaker classical-trace branch: u is C2 inside Omega, u and all first derivatives extend continuously to its closure, f=(-Delta-k²)u belongs to L1(Omega), and the equation holds inside. The boundary values and normal derivative in the formula below are these actual continuous traces. Then
$$u(x)=\int_\Omega G_k(x-y)f(y)\,dy+\int_{\partial\Omega}\bigl[G_k(x-y)\partial_nu(y)-u(y)\partial_{n_y}G_k(x-y)\bigr]dS_y,$$
with n the outward domain normal; both integrals are absolutely convergent. Merely being smooth on the OPEN domain without these trace/integrability data is insufficient.

For an exterior D=R3 minus closure of a bounded smooth obstacle, retain the exterior counterpart with actual inner boundary traces: suppose u is C2 on D with u and first derivatives continuous to its compact boundary, solves (-Delta-k²)u=f there, f is locally continuous and $\int_D|G_k(x-y)f(y)|dy$ is finite at the observation x, and the prescribed outgoing condition gives, uniformly on spheres at infinity, $u(y)=O(|y|^{-1})$ and $\partial_ru(y)-iku(y)=o(|y|^{-1})$. Then the same formula holds with volume D and its obstacle boundary, with n outward from D (pointing into the obstacle). Compactly supported L1 sources with the displayed local regularity are a sufficient source subclass. For the smooth-trace modal outgoing specialization beyond a source-containing sphere of radius $R_0>0$, retain the declared full Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for this sufficient branch. Write the smooth angular trace as $g(n)=u(R_0n)$, use the real unit-sphere harmonics of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], set $c_{lm}=\int_{S^2}g(n)Y_{lm}(n)d\Omega(n)$, and define the outgoing modal class outside that sphere by
$$u(rn)=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}c_{lm}\,\frac{h_l(kr)}{h_l(kR_0)}Y_{lm}(n),\qquad r\ge R_0,$$
where $h_l$ are exactly the earlier explicit functions of [[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]. The proof below establishes smooth convergence, the homogeneous exterior equation, the actual trace g, the uniform bound $\sup_{r\ge R_0,n\in S^2}r|u(rn)|<\infty$ and the uniform Sommerfeld residual $\sup_{n\in S^2}r|\partial_ru(rn)-iku(rn)|\to0$. Thus this existing smooth modal branch satisfies the prescribed far conditions without a later same-page supplier. Its full-Choice premise is retained; the earlier prescribed-outgoing branch remains under Countable Choice.

The Green formula uses the consistent actual pair of traces. Assigning both aperture values independently does not establish an exact boundary problem; a declared scalar aperture-source model remains a separate approximation. No weak boundary trace or normal trace for arbitrary rough data is asserted by mere interior smoothness.
before.strategy:
For the closure-smooth bounded specialization, apply [[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] on Omega with a small ball about x removed. The k² terms cancel, the outgoing kernel's unit inner flux gives u(x), and its derivative-test term is O(delta); the source integral near x is finite since f is continuous there and G_k is locally integrable. This proves the stated signs.

For the weaker C2-interior/C1-closure trace branch, let S be the compact smooth boundary with its outward normal n. The exact [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]] under Countable Choice gives a normal tube with positive smooth radius; compactness gives a positive minimum. For sufficiently small t>0, $S_t=\{p-t n(p):p\in S\}$ lies inside Omega and bounds the inner domain Omega_t. In the normal graph charts the surface Jacobian and outward normals converge uniformly to those on S (the differential of p to p-tn(p) tends uniformly to the tangent identity). The one-sided graph convention makes this the actual inside collar; injectivity of the tube prevents overlap. For small t, x and a fixed ball about x lie in Omega_t. On each punctured Omega_t the ordinary Green theorem applies, since u is C2 on a neighbourhood of its compact closure. First remove the x-excision radius by the same local flux argument. Then take t down0: u and its gradient converge uniformly on S_t to their continuous actual traces, while G_k and its y-gradient are bounded and smooth on this collar away from x. The boundary integrals therefore converge to exactly the displayed trace integrals using the compact surface chart formula and the uniformly converging Jacobians. For the volume term, split off a small ball about x, where f is bounded and the kernel is integrable; on its complement G_k is bounded and f is L1. This gives an absolute integrable majorant, so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] on the increasing inner domains yields the full volume integral. This proves the weaker branch completely rather than assuming unspecified traces.

For the exterior branch, truncate by B_R and use the same inner-boundary trace limit and x-excision argument, with the outward obstacle normal pointing into the obstacle. For fixed observation x, on y=Rn the explicit kernel has $G_k(x-y)=O(R^{-1})$ and $\partial_R G_k(x-y)-ikG_k(x-y)=O(R^{-2})$, uniformly in n; these follow by differentiating the norm and $\partial_R|Rn-x|=1+O(R^{-2})$. In the outer Wronskian, write $G_k(\partial_Ru-iku)-u(\partial_RG_k-ikG_k)$: its supremum is o(R^-2)+O(R^-3), so multiplying by the sphere area O(R²) makes it tend to0. Absolute convergence of the stated volume integral then permits the limit R to infinity. The smooth-trace modal outgoing subclass has the explicit earlier-supplier proof below; its existing full-Choice sufficient premise is retained. Other prescribed uniform-outgoing data use only Countable Choice through Green, tubular and surface interfaces. No independent assignment of both boundary traces or unproved rough-trace Green theorem is used. The cited Green theorem has real inputs; apply it to the four real/imaginary component pairs and combine by complex bilinearity to obtain the displayed complex kernel identity, with no conjugation introduced.

Smooth angular coefficient estimate from finite angular calculus. For smooth w on S2 let $L_jw(n)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}w(Q_j(t)n)\right|_{t=0}$, where $Q_j(t)$ is the elementary coordinate rotation about e_j, and put $\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^3L_j^2$. Its tangent velocity is $e_j\times n$ with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. Rotation invariance of surface measure is the exact earlier [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]. Differentiate the invariant integral of w(Q_j(t)n)v(Q_j(t)n) on the compact sphere: uniform difference quotients of its smooth integrand give $\int(L_jw)v=-\int w(L_jv)$, so Lambda is symmetric under the bilinear integral; for complex data apply the same finite identity to components. No polar-operator theorem is presumed. On an ambient smooth extension, direct coordinate differentiation gives
$$\sum_jL_j^2=|x|^2\Delta-(x\cdot\nabla)^2-x\cdot\nabla.$$
Each Y_lm is the restriction of a degree-l homogeneous harmonic polynomial by the earlier H2 supplier, so Euler's identity and this finite formula give $\Lambda Y_{lm}=-l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Therefore, for l>=1 and any integer p>=1, repeated symmetry and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] yield
$$[l(l+1)]^p c_{lm}=\int_{S^2}(-\Lambda)^pg\,Y_{lm}\,d\Omega,\qquad |c_{lm}|\le\frac{\|\Lambda^pg\|_2}{[l(l+1)]^p}.$$
The smooth g and all these angular derivatives are bounded on the compact sphere and have finite L2 norms. Treat l0 separately as its single finite constant coefficient. The addition diagonal of H2 gives $\|Y_{lm}\|_\infty\le\sqrt{(2l+1)/(4\pi)}$. With p2, the total weighted absolute sum
$$\sum_{l,m}(l+1+2kR_0)|c_{lm}|\,\|Y_{lm}\|_\infty<\infty$$
follows: for l>=1 its degree-l bound is a fixed constant times $(2l+1)(l+1+2kR_0)\sqrt{(2l+1)/(4\pi)}[l(l+1)]^{-2}=O(l^{-3/2})$. This is the actual summability argument for every smooth trace, not an unproved claim of coefficient decay.

Exact radial majorants. From the earlier Hankel proof, $F_l(z)=z^2|h_l(z)|^2=\sum_{j=0}^la_jz^{-2j}$ has a0=1 and positive a_j, so it is nonincreasing in z>0. Consequently, for $\phi_l(r)=h_l(kr)/h_l(kR_0)$,
$$|\phi_l(r)|\le R_0/r\quad(r\ge R_0).$$
The same earlier supplier's exact t_l bounds, applied with radius r, give $|k h_l'(kr)/h_l(kr)|\le(l+1)/r+k$, hence
$$r|\phi_l'(r)-ik\phi_l(r)|\le R_0[(l+1)/r+2k]\le l+1+2kR_0.$$
For every FIXED l the explicit finite outgoing polynomial gives $r(\phi_l'-ik\phi_l)\to0$ as r tends infinity. The weighted coefficient sum therefore bounds every residual tail uniformly for ALL r>=R0 and n on the sphere. Given epsilon, choose a finite degree cutoff making that tail smaller than epsilon/2; the finitely many remaining radial residuals tend to0 uniformly after multiplication by their fixed finite angular suprema. This finite-head/finite-tail argument proves the uniform Sommerfeld limit. Also $r|u(rn)|\le R_0\sum|c_{lm}|\|Y_{lm}\|_\infty$ uniformly, which proves exactly the amplitude bound used in the outer Green Wronskian. The first radial derivative series is uniformly convergent on r>=R0 since $|\phi_l'|\le[(l+1)/R_0+k]|\phi_l|$ and the same weighted sum dominates it; finite-coordinate FTC [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]] identifies that derivative with partial_r u.

Smooth modal realization and normalization. Rotational differentiation preserves the degree-l harmonic space. Skew symmetry gives $\sum_j\|L_jv\|_2^2=l(l+1)\|v\|_2^2$ in that finite space, so each successive angular derivative has norm at most [l(l+1)]^(1/2) times the preceding norm. Its pointwise norm is bounded by sqrt((2l+1)/(4pi)) times its L2 norm by finite basis Cauchy-Schwarz and the addition identity. The radial ODE of the earlier Hankel supplier, differentiated finitely many times, gives for every fixed q a bound $|\phi_l^{(q)}(r)|\le C_{q,k,R_0}(l+1)^{2q}/r$ on r>=R0: q0 is the radial-ratio bound, q1 is the logarithmic-derivative bound, and the equation plus derivatives of r^-1,r^-2 gives the induction. Thus every radial/angular derivative series is dominated by a finite power of l times the coefficient estimate with a sufficiently large p. It converges uniformly on each closed bounded exterior annulus; FTC identifies all derivatives. Cartesian derivatives there are finite combinations of radial and angular derivatives with smooth coefficients (from $\nabla=n\partial_r-r^{-1}n\times(L_1,L_2,L_3)$), so the series defines a smooth exterior field. The finite angular identity above gives the polar Laplacian formula on phi_l(r)Y_lm, and the radial ODE makes each term solve (Delta+k²)u0; termwise second derivatives prove the equation for the limit. At rR0 the absolute series has its L2 coefficients c_lm; completeness of H2 and continuity give its actual smooth trace g. If trace coefficients are recorded instead in the sphere-normalized basis $Y^{R_0}_{lm}(R_0n)=R_0^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, their coefficients are R0 c_lm, so the displayed expansion is identical after normalization. No weaker rough-trace claim or obstacle-boundary existence is inferred. All bounded Green, weaker C1-trace, exterior source and smooth-modal conclusions are preserved, with the same declared Choice strengths.

before.title: Outgoing spherical trace and Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers. Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y^R_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion. Here the boundary Sobolev spaces are their complex versions (or complexifications of the real trace spaces), $f_{lm}=\int_{S_R}f\overline{Y^R_{lm}}\,d\sigma_R$, and the DtN dual pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.
before.strategy: The boundary norm of the fractional Sobolev space is equivalent, for fixed $R$, to $\sum_{l,m}(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$: for finite harmonic data the harmonic ball extension $\sum_{l,m}(r/R)^lf_{lm}R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ has Dirichlet energy $\sum(l/R)|f_{lm}|^2$ by the first Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) and normal differentiation, and $L^2$ ball norm $\sum R/(2l+3)|f_{lm}|^2$ with the sphere-normalised basis, so its $H^1$ norm is equivalent to $\sum(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$. For arbitrary $H^{1/2}$ data the bounded right inverse and the weak harmonic Dirichlet solver of the prescribed-data lemma ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]) give a controlled harmonic $H^1$ extension; the harmonic coefficients and orthogonality of the ball Poisson series lemma ([[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]]) show the finite energy partial sums are bounded by its energy, giving both directions of the equivalence. The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. For the exterior realisation, define $u_{lm}(r)=f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)$, $r\ge R$; the finite polynomial positive formula gives $|h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)|\le R/r$ and, by the recurrence, geometric-in-$l$ radial ratios on every compact $r>R$ interval, so the series and all derivatives converge uniformly there, away from the sphere; the smoothness, the weak trace identification and the annular $H^1$ control follow from Green's identity for each mode on $[R,R+\delta]$ and the bounds above. Uniqueness: the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of $h_l(kr)$ and its incoming partner, whose Wronskian is nonzero; Sommerfeld selects $h_l$, and harmonic completeness forces any smooth outgoing exterior solution to have exactly this map. The annular $H^1$ estimates are precisely the finite-local-energy condition; they do not assert global integrability at infinity. At $l=0$, a nonzero outgoing mode is proportional to $e^{ikr}/r$ and its global $L^2$ norm diverges, which confirms why no global energy condition is imposed. Both the ball and exterior radial extensions use $R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ explicitly; the sphere-normalisation is $Y^R_{lm}(Rn)=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, giving the stated radial ball-norm factor $R/(2l+3)$ for the sphere-normalised coefficients. For complex boundary data, apply the real prescribed-trace/harmonic solver to the real and imaginary parts and combine; the resulting squared norm is the sum of the two real energy norms, with the stated sesquilinear pairing.

after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers. Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y^R_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion. Here the boundary Sobolev spaces are their complex versions (or complexifications of the real trace spaces), $f_{lm}=\int_{S_R}f\overline{Y^R_{lm}}\,d\sigma_R$, and the DtN dual pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.
after.strategy: The boundary norm of the fractional Sobolev space is equivalent, for fixed $R$, to $\sum_{l,m}(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$: for finite harmonic data the harmonic ball extension $\sum_{l,m}(r/R)^lf_{lm}R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ has Dirichlet energy $\sum(l/R)|f_{lm}|^2$ by the first Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) and normal differentiation, and $L^2$ ball norm $\sum R/(2l+3)|f_{lm}|^2$ with the sphere-normalised basis, so its $H^1$ norm is equivalent to $\sum(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$. For arbitrary $H^{1/2}$ data the bounded right inverse and the weak harmonic Dirichlet solver of the prescribed-data lemma ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]) give a controlled harmonic $H^1$ extension; the harmonic coefficients and orthogonality of the ball Poisson series lemma ([[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]]) show the finite energy partial sums are bounded by its energy, giving both directions of the equivalence. The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. For the exterior realisation, define $u_{lm}(r)=f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)$, $r\ge R$; the finite polynomial positive formula gives $|h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)|\le R/r$ and, by the recurrence, geometric-in-$l$ radial ratios on every compact $r>R$ interval, so the series and all derivatives converge uniformly there, away from the sphere; the smoothness, the weak trace identification and the annular $H^1$ control follow from Green's identity for each mode on $[R,R+\delta]$ and the bounds above. Uniqueness: the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of $h_l(kr)$ and its incoming partner, whose Wronskian is nonzero; Sommerfeld selects $h_l$, and harmonic completeness forces any smooth outgoing exterior solution to have exactly this map. The annular $H^1$ estimates are precisely the finite-local-energy condition; they do not assert global integrability at infinity. At $l=0$, a nonzero outgoing mode is proportional to $e^{ikr}/r$ and its global $L^2$ norm diverges, which confirms why no global energy condition is imposed. Both the ball and exterior radial extensions use $R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ explicitly; the sphere-normalisation is $Y^R_{lm}(Rn)=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, giving the stated radial ball-norm factor $R/(2l+3)$ for the sphere-normalised coefficients. For complex boundary data, apply the real prescribed-trace/harmonic solver to the real and imaginary parts and combine; the resulting squared norm is the sum of the two real energy norms, with the stated sesquilinear pairing.

before.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J:=rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component is J^0=rho_0 U^0. Future timelikeness gives U^0>0 in every inertial chart, so define the normalized chart direction u:=U/U^0 and the coordinate density rho:=J^0. Then u^0=1, u^i=U^i/U^0, rho=rho_0 U^0, and J=rho u pointwise. The coordinate density rho and scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: rho=rho_0 if and only if rho_0(U^0−1)=0; at points where rho_0!=0 equality holds exactly when U^0=1. The vector u is a normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity normalization. In an x^0=ct convention the associated spatial coordinate velocity, if interpreted as such, has components c u^i; physical current/density identification requires its own model premise. Interpretation boundary: the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field, and of rho with a measured charge density, is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert that any physical current transforms as a vector.
before.strategy: Proof plan. (i) and (ii) are the definitions of components: for a vector field, J'(p) = sum_a J'^a(p) partial'_a|_p and partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b, so comparing coefficients with J = sum_b J^b partial_b gives J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b; the covector transform is the dual statement k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b. The affine phase invariance in (ii) is the displayed substitution k_a x^a = k'_c x'^c - k'_c b^c. (iii) is the multilinear evaluation: writing T(p) on the transformed basis and using the definition of the components, each contravariant slot contributes Lambda and each covariant slot the inverse; the contraction claim follows from (Lambda^{-1})^a_b Lambda^b_c = delta^a_c, and eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} is the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property of Lambda. (iv) is the chain rule for the transition x' = Lambda x + b: partial'_a = (partial x^c / partial x'^a) partial_c = (Lambda^{-1})^c_a partial_c; substituting into partial'_a J'^a and using (i) gives the invariance of the divergence, and the (2,0) case follows by the same substitution with the two contravariant factors. (v) An alternating covariant field is a covariant tensor field, so the slot-by-slot covariant law applies; for the volume form, which by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form is the determinant of the coordinate matrix in an oriented frame, the transformation multiplies the determinant by det(Lambda^{-1}) = 1, and by det Lambda = -1 in the improper case. (vi) is the matrix multiplication of the boost matrix with the component vector; (vii) A future timelike vector has positive time component in any oriented inertial chart. Thus U^0 is nonzero and u:=U/U^0 is well-defined, with u^0=1 and u^i=U^i/U^0. Componentwise multiplication gives J^0=rho_0 U^0=:rho and J=rho_0 U=rho_0 U^0(U/U^0)=rho u. Therefore rho−rho_0=rho_0(U^0−1), giving precisely the asserted equality cases, including rho_0=0. C^1 regularity of J follows by the componentwise product rule. The normalized chart direction generally has neither four-velocity norm−c² nor unit norm−1; in x^0=ct a curve tangent proportional to U has dx^i/dt=c U^i/U^0=c u^i. No measured-density or physical-current assertion is inferred from this algebra. The item must not claim that a physical current is a vector field: that adoption belongs to the electromagnetic model, and the final paragraph of the statement records the boundary. All computations are finite algebra and the chain rule for total derivatives.

before.title: Worked motion of the primed frame's origin under a passive boost
before.statement: Worked computation. Let B = B(beta e_1) be a passive boost with parameter beta in (-1,1) along the first spatial direction of an inertial frame with coordinates (x^0,x^1) (def-lorentz-boost). Then: (i) The worldline x'^1 = 0, x'^2 = a, x'^3 = b of the primed chart's origin (up to the fixed transverse coordinates) is, in the unprimed chart, x^1 = beta x^0 with x^2, x^3 arbitrary constants: indeed x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - beta x^0) = 0 forces x^1 = beta x^0, and the transverse coordinates are unchanged because B fixes them. With x^0 = c t this is uniform motion with coordinate velocity beta c along e_1. (ii) Conversely the unprimed origin x^1 = 0 satisfies x'^1 = gamma(0 - beta x^0) = -beta gamma x^0 = -beta x'^0, since x'^0 = gamma x^0 when x^1 = 0; so the unprimed frame moves with parameter -beta in the primed chart, consistent with B^{-1} = B(-beta). (iii) For beta = 3/5 the concrete values are x^1 = (3/5)x^0 in the first chart and x'^1 = -(3/5)x'^0 in the second; the worldline x'^1 = 0 passes through the event (x^0,x^1) = (0,0) and through (5,3) (choosing x^0 = 5), which the boost maps to (x'^0,x'^1) = (5/4)(5 - (3/5)3), (5/4)(3 - (3/5)5) = (4,0), confirming x'^1 = 0.
before.strategy: The computation solves the linear equation x'^1 = 0 for x^1 and evaluates the inverse boost; both are finite rational computations. The physical reading of beta c as a velocity is not part of this mathematical example and is recorded on the page's physics theorem; the identity x^1 = beta x^0 is the coordinate statement that the primed chart's spatial origin moves, which is why the parameter beta is called the boost parameter.

before.title: The localized Newtonian potential and the ideal point-charge Coulomb field
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in $\mathbb R^3$ with its Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}>0$. Let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ fundamental solution of $-\Delta$ of [[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], normalised by $-\Delta T_\Phi=\delta_0$; then $\omega_2=4\pi$ and
$$\Phi(z)=\frac{1}{4\pi|z|}\qquad(z\ne0)$$
([[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). Let $Nf$ be the Newtonian potential of [[def-newtonian-potential]].
(a) [Smooth compact sources] Let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with compact support contained in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), put $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi$. Then $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[thm-newtonian-potential-for-holder-data-is-classical]]), and pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$
$$-\Delta\varphi=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0$$
with the operators of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]] and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Moreover, with $Q:=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Coulomb integral representation holds, and its far-field bound holds for $|x|>2R$,
$$E(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{x-y}{|x-y|^3}\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(x\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad |E(x)|\le\frac{\| \rho\|_1}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}\quad(|x|>2R),$$
and for $|x|>\max(2R,1)$ the potential obeys the decay bound $|\varphi(x)|\le\bigl(|Q|/(4\pi)+R\|\rho\|_1/\pi\bigr)/(\varepsilon_0|x|)$ ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]], [[thm-decay-of-the-newtonian-potential-of-compactly-supported-data]]). The pair $(E,0,\rho,0)$ therefore realises the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with source $\rho$, and $E$ is the field of the localised Newtonian potential.
(b) [Uniqueness with vanishing at infinity] If $\psi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $-\Delta\psi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$ and $\lim_{|x|\to\infty}\psi(x)=0$, then $\psi=\varphi$ ([[thm-weak-maximum-principle-for-the-laplacian]]). In particular, among $C^2$ solutions of the Poisson equation of a compactly supported $C^1$ source decaying at infinity, the localised Newtonian potential is the unique one.
(c) [Compactly supported $L^1$ sources] If instead $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ is real, measurable and compactly supported, then $N\rho$ is finite $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere, belongs to $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, is $C^\infty$ and harmonic off the support of $\rho$, and its regular distribution satisfies
$$-\Delta T_{\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho}=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally]], scaled by $\varepsilon_0^{-1}$; [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).

before.title: The flat covariant derivative on affine Minkowski space and fields along curves
before.statement:

For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. The value does not depend on the inertial chart: for another inertial chart x' = Lambda x + b one has partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b and Y'^a = Lambda^a_b Y^b (thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation), and Lambda is constant, so (Lambda^{-1})^a_c X'^b partial'_b Y'^c = X^b partial_b Y^a. nabla_X Y is again a smooth vector field. (b) Covector and general tensor fields. For a smooth covector field alpha set (nabla_X alpha)(Y) := X(alpha(Y)) - alpha(nabla_X Y); for a type (r,s) tensor field T define nabla_X T by the derivation rule on the evaluation of T on smooth vector and covector fields, subtracting the covariant derivative of each vector argument and also subtracting the covariant derivative of each covector argument; Precisely, for $T:(V^*)^r	imes V^s	o\mathbb R$, $(
abla_XT)(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)=X[T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)]-\sum_iT(\alpha_1,\ldots,
abla_X\alpha_i,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,Y_s)-\sum_jT(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r;Y_1,\ldots,
abla_XY_j,\ldots,Y_s)$. In inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of that component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation. (e) First-order C1 version. For C1 vector fields X,Y and C1 covector/tensor fields on Omega, the same directional/evaluation definitions are well-defined and have continuous coefficients: in an inertial chart $(
abla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$ and each tensor component is differentiated in the same way. The component recovery and subtraction of all argument derivatives remain valid. C1 scalar multiplication satisfies the same first-order Leibniz rules, metric compatibility remains $
abla\eta=0$, and the first-order torsion identity uses the continuous coordinate bracket $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$. No C1 closure of this bracket or second covariant derivative of arbitrary C1 data is asserted. For C2 vector fields the second derivatives needed for the zero-curvature identity in(c) exist, and that identity follows by equality of the continuous mixed second partials. All original smooth-field properties and the C1 along-curve derivative in(d) are retained.

(i) The directional derivative in (a) is the derivative of the V-valued composite t |-> Y(p+tX(p)); its coordinate expression is the chain rule, and chart independence is the corrected identity X'^b partial'_b Y'^a=Lambda^a_c X^b partial_b Y^c, equivalently inverse-Lambda recovery of the unprimed components, using that inertial transitions are affine (their second derivatives vanish, so no inhomogeneous term appears) and their linear parts are constant. (ii) The extension in(b) subtracts the derivative of every argument, whether vector or covector. In an inertial chart use the constant coordinate basis and constant dual basis; their covariant derivatives vanish, so evaluating the rule on those bases leaves only X acting on each tensor component. For variable arguments the ordinary product rule cancels all their derivatives with the displayed subtractions. This proves the stated coordinate formula and the evaluation derivation rule; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts. (iii) The properties in (c) are coordinate computations: torsion-freeness is X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a = [X,Y]^a, zero curvature is the interchange of mixed partials, and metric compatibility is the constancy of the component matrix eta_{ab}. (iv) In (d), the canonical isomorphism T_pA = V is independent of p, so the covariant derivative along a curve coincides with the ordinary derivative and parallel transport is trivial; this is exactly what makes Fermi-Walker transport below an ordinary linear ODE. before.title: Fermi-Walker transport along a timelike worldline
before.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U = dx/dtau and four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), so eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition), and let X: I -> V be a C^1 field along x (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve). (a) The Fermi-Walker derivative of X is D_FW X/dtau := X' - (1/c^2)(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A), where X' is the ordinary V-valued derivative of X (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)). X is Fermi-Walker transported along x when D_FW X/dtau = 0, i.e. when X' = (1/c^2)(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A). (b) The four-velocity is Fermi-Walker transported: D_FW U/dtau = A - (1/c^2)(eta(A,U)U - eta(U,U)A) = A - A = 0, using eta(U,A) = 0 and eta(U,U) = -c^2. (c) If A = 0 on an interval then Fermi-Walker transport coincides there with ordinary (parallel) transport X' = 0; if A is not zero, the definition includes exactly the correction that transports the time leg U/c itself. (d) A Fermi-Walker transported tetrad along x is a tuple (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3) of C^1 fields along x with E_0 = U/c and every E_a Fermi-Walker transported; existence from a prescribed initial tetrad and preservation of the tetrad conditions are proved in the following lemma. The physical interpretation (a nonrotating spatial frame carried by an accelerated observer) is not asserted here; only the transport rule is defined.

(ii) The identity in (b) is a short computation using eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 from thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (iii) The contrast with parallel transport in (c) is immediate from the definition, and (d) fixes terminology. (iv) Existence, uniqueness and preservation properties are deliberately not claimed here; they are supplied by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness and thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples. after.title: Fermi-Walker transport along a timelike worldline
after.statement:
Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline with four-velocity $U=dx/d\tau$ and four-acceleration $A=dU/d\tau$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), so that $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]), write $s$ for its given parameter and $\tau$ for its proper-time function, with $\tau'(s)>0$, and let $X:I\to V$ be a $C^1$ field along $x$ ([[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]]).

**(a) Fermi–Walker derivative.** The **Fermi–Walker derivative of $X$** is

$$\frac{D_{\mathrm{FW}}X}{d\tau}:=\frac{X'}{\tau'}-\frac{1}{c^2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr),$$

where $X'$ denotes differentiation with respect to $s$ and $dX/d\tau:=X'/\tau'$. Here $\tau'=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}>0$ by [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]. The derivative $X'$ is the ordinary $V$-valued derivative of $X$, which is the covariant derivative of $X$ along $x$ in the flat model ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], clause (d)). The field $X$ is **Fermi–Walker transported along $x$** when $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=0$, that is, when

$$X'=\frac{\tau'}{c^2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr).$$

**(b) The four-velocity is Fermi–Walker transported.** Substituting $X=U$ and using $\eta(A,U)=0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ gives $D_{\mathrm{FW}}U/d\tau=U'/\tau'-c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,U)U-\eta(U,U)A\bigr)=A-A=0$.

**(c) Comparison with parallel transport.** If $A=0$ on an interval $J\subseteq I$, then on $J$ the Fermi–Walker equation reduces to $X'=0$ and coincides with ordinary parallel transport; if $A$ is not zero, the definition includes exactly the correction that also transports the time leg $U/c$ along the worldline.

**(d) Fermi–Walker transported tetrad.** A **Fermi–Walker transported tetrad along $x$** is a tuple $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of $C^1$ fields along $x$ with $E_0=U/c$ and with every $E_a$ Fermi–Walker transported along $x$. Existence from a prescribed initial tetrad and preservation of the tetrad conditions under this transport are proved in the following lemma. The physical interpretation as a nonrotating spatial frame carried by an accelerated observer is not asserted here; only the transport rule is defined.

(ii) The identity in (b) is a short computation using eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 from thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. before.title: Existence, uniqueness and linearity of Fermi-Walker transport
before.statement: Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U and four-acceleration A, let tau_0 be in I and X_0 in V. Then there is exactly one C^1 field X: I -> V along x with D_FW X/dtau = 0 and X(tau_0) = X_0; if x is C^k with k >= 2 then X is C^{k-1}. The map X_0 |-> X from V to the C^1 fields along x satisfying the transport equation is linear. Consequently, for every tetrad (E_0(tau_0),...,E_3(tau_0)) at x(tau_0) with E_0(tau_0) = U(tau_0)/c there is a unique tuple of Fermi-Walker transported fields with those initial values; whether that tuple remains a tetrad at every time is proved in the following item.
before.strategy: (i) In an inertial chart the equation reads X'^a = M^a{}_b(tau) X^b with M^a{}_b(tau) = c^{-2}(U^a(tau)A_b(tau) - A^a(tau)U_b(tau)), a continuous matrix-valued function on the interval I because x is C^2. (ii) On each compact subinterval [a,b] of I containing tau_0, lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval gives a unique solution with the prescribed initial value; uniqueness on overlaps makes the local solutions agree, so they define a unique solution on all of I (I is an increasing union of compact subintervals; equivalently use def-maximal-ode-solution and thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution). (iii) Linearity in the initial value follows from uniqueness applied to linear combinations of solutions; the regularity statement follows because the right-hand side M X is C^{k-2} when x is C^k, so the solution gains one derivative. No choice principle is used.

before.title: Fermi-Walker transport preserves the metric, and explicit rigid and non-rigid observer congruences
before.statement: (a) Preservation. Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline and let X,Y: I -> V be C^1 Fermi-Walker transported fields along x (def-sr-fermi-walker-transport). Then tau |-> eta(X(tau),Y(tau)) is constant on I; in particular Fermi-Walker transport preserves norms and orthogonality, and the unique Fermi-Walker transported family with initial values a tetrad (E_0(tau_0),...,E_3(tau_0)) with E_0(tau_0) = U(tau_0)/c is an orthonormal tetrad (E_0(tau),...,E_3(tau)) at every tau with E_0(tau) = U(tau)/c (observer-adapted tetrad), by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Rindler wedge congruence. In an inertial chart (x^0,x,y,z) consider Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2, with theta in R and rho>0. Then Phi is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge W := {(x^0,x) : x > |x^0|}, with smooth inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)); the pullback of eta is g = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2; the field n := rho^{-1} partial/partial theta is a future unit timelike field on W whose congruence is Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial/partial rho, hence eta(a,a) = rho^{-2}; its rest slices theta = const are hyperplanes orthogonal to n with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 independent of theta; and the frame (n, partial/partial rho, partial/partial y, partial/partial z) is a tetrad field which is not a coordinate frame, since [n, partial/partial rho] = +(1/rho) n is nonzero (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). (c) Rigid rotation, ambient nonintegrability and ring holonomy. Fix real Omega. In the inertial chart let U_Omega be the open timelike region r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2<c^2/Omega^2 when Omega!=0, and the whole chart when Omega=0. On this four-dimensional open set put K=partial_0+(Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1+x^1 partial_2), gamma(r)=(1-Omega^2 r^2/c^2)^(-1/2), and n=gamma(r)K. This is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence. If Omega!=0, its three-dimensional rest distribution in the ambient open set is nowhere integrable: its vorticity is nowhere zero and no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. If Omega=0, n=partial_0 is inertial and irrotational, and the rest hypersurfaces are x^0=const. Now fix R>0 with |Omega|R<c and restrict to the timelike ring cylinder r=R, x^3=const, whose rotating angle is varphi=phi-Omega t modulo2pi, x^0=ct. The ring observer phi=phi_0+Omega t has n=gamma(R)(1,-(Omega R/c)sin phi,(Omega R/c)cos phi,0). The induced metric is -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2Omega R^2 dt dvarphi+R^2 dvarphi^2. The ambient rest covector restricted to the cylinder is proportional to -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt+Omega R^2 dvarphi, so the one-dimensional rest distribution on that cylinder is locally integrable and satisfies dt/dvarphi=Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). After one positive circuit in the rotating label, its lift starting at t=0 has signed time offset Delta t=2pi Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). For Omega!=0 it returns to the same rotating label at a different time and does not close as a ring rest-simultaneity curve; there is no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time on the entire cylinder with time-oriented nonzero differential annihilating these rest lines. This global ring holonomy is distinct from the ambient local Frobenius obstruction. For Omega=0 the offset is zero and ring rest lines are t=const. (d) Bell first-order field. Let q: J -> R^3 be C^2 with q(t) = (q_1(t),0,0) and |q_1'(t)| < c, and consider the C1 future unit field of the translated worldlines x_xi(t) = (c t, q(t) + xi) parametrized by xi in an open subset of R^3, with n = gamma(1, q_1'(t)/c, 0, 0), gamma = (1 - q_1'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and unit longitudinal rest vector s = gamma(q_1'(t)/c, 1, 0, 0). For this C1 field define the first-order rest projection $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ and projected deformation $\theta_{ab}=h^c{}_a h^d{}_b\partial_{(c}n_{d)}$, using the explicit first-order version of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space. These coordinate formulas need only C1 n, give a continuous tensor, and agree with the smooth congruence definitions when q is smooth; in this first-order sense Born rigidity means theta=0. Then theta(s,s) = s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 q_1'(t) q_1''(t)/c^3, which is nonzero exactly when q_1'(t) q_1''(t) is nonzero; hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a parameter value with q_1'(t) q_1''(t) nonzero, although for every fixed chart time t the separation between the members labelled xi_1 and xi_2 is the constant |xi_1 - xi_2|. The Omega=0 limit has the constant unit field. On the ring cylinder, substitute x^0=ct, x^1=Rcos(varphi+Omega t), x^2=Rsin(varphi+Omega t) to obtain the displayed metric and covector. Its one-dimensional kernel is the line field generated by partial_varphi+[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]partial_t, whose integral gives the signed holonomy. A globally defined time-oriented rest-synchronization function would have differential a positive multiple of dt-[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]dvarphi. Its integral around a fixed-t ring would have nonzero constant sign for Omega!=0, contradicting exactness of that differential. No local nonintegrability is attributed to the cylinder's one-dimensional rest-line field. (d) C2 q makes q1' C1, gamma C1 and n C1. Use the explicitly given first-order projected symmetric derivative of n; no smooth-only congruence or later connecting-field theorem is invoked. Write beta=q_1'/c, beta'=q_1''/c, x^0=ct and n_b=(-gamma,gamma beta,0,0), so partial_0=(1/c)d/dt and partial_1 n_b=0. Differentiation gives partial_0 n_0=-gamma^3 beta beta'/c and partial_0 n_1=gamma^3 beta'/c, using 1+gamma^2 beta^2=gamma^2. Contract with s=(gamma beta,gamma,0,0): s^0[s^0 partial_0 n_0+s^1 partial_0 n_1]=gamma^5 beta beta'(1-beta^2)/c=gamma^3 beta beta'/c=gamma^3 q_1' q_1''/c^3. Projection to the rest space does not change this contraction since s is rest-orthogonal. All transverse expansion components vanish, so it is nonzero exactly under the stated condition, and fixed chart-time separations remain xi_1-xi_2. The material fracture conclusion is excluded. All computations use finite algebra and the declared calculus, with no choice principle.

(a) x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and x = rho cosh theta > 0 give that the image is the right wedge W = {x > |x^0|}, and the inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2)log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)) is smooth on W; both maps are smooth, so Phi is a diffeomorphism onto W. (b) Differentiating gives dx^0 = sinh theta d rho + rho cosh theta d theta and dx = cosh theta d rho + rho sinh theta d theta, so the pullback metric is -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2. (c) The field n := rho^{-1} partial_theta satisfies eta(n,n) = -1 and is future. Computing with the pullback metric, the nonzero connection coefficients are Gamma^rho_{theta theta} = rho and Gamma^theta_{theta rho} = Gamma^theta_{rho theta} = 1/rho, so nabla_{partial_theta} partial_theta = rho partial_rho and the congruence acceleration is a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho, with eta(a,a) = 1/rho^2; for example at rho = 2 one has |a| = 1/2 in reciprocal-length units. (d) The slices theta = const are hyperplanes through the origin with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, independent of theta; hence the congruence is Born rigid. It is also irrotational: the rest distribution is the tangent distribution of the theta-slices, hence integrable, and omega = 0 by thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius. (e) The tetrad field (n, partial_rho, partial_y, partial_z) is not a coordinate frame: [n, partial_rho] = [rho^{-1}partial_theta, partial_rho] = +(1/rho^2) partial_theta = +(1/rho) n is nonzero, and a coordinate frame's members commute (def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction). This realizes the Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples with exact formulas.
